I organized the 100 experiments as 14 controlled contrasts. Each contrast applies one fixed edit to parents that differ in a single condition, so any difference in the measured effect can be attributed to that condition. Most parents are all-`nor_conv_3x3` or all-`skip_connect` with one or two edges changed.

The contrasts target the interactions most likely in this cell topology:

- **Path redundancy:** whether edge 3 (direct input to output) or edge 5 is `none`, which changes how much the other paths matter.
- **Dead branches:** whether node 1 or node 2 has any consumer or producer. For example, editing edge 0 when edges 2 and 4 are both `none` should do almost nothing.
- **Op being replaced:** the same edit applied to edges currently holding none, skip, pool, 1x1 or 3x3.
- **Background op:** the same edit in conv-heavy versus skip-heavy versus pool-heavy cells.
